Hokuriku, along the northern coast of Honshū, is one of the most prosperous regions of Japan. Home to some of the wealthiest domains in Japan, especially the Maeda of Kaga, the single wealthiest domain in all of Japan, Hokuriku produces a great deal of the rice used to feed central Honshū. Hokuriku is almost entirely loyal to the Shogunate, with most domains either staying loyal throughout the future Boshin War or refusing to take side. However, their reluctance to reform has placed the domains of Hokuriku in the backseat, becoming less relevant than the poorer but more fiery domains in the southwest and north. || Ezo (modern Hokkaidō), home to the Ainu, remained a remote frontier. In the late Bakumatsu, the Matsumae Domain managed small garrisons and fortified trading posts to assert shogunate influence, while Ainu communities maintained autonomous governance. The region was a delicate frontier where indigenous autonomy, limited shogunate oversight, and foreign concerns, particularly Russian encroachment, intersected.
